title: Rotini Configuration Schema
description: Schema for a Rotini CLI configuration file.

$schema.description: URL identifying the rotini configuration schema version. The version segment must match the installed rotini binary version.

GenerateHelpConfig.description: Controls generation of embedded, per-command help text.

enabled.description: When true, rotini seeds a per-command help .txt file (containing the command name) for any command that lacks one, then embeds every command's help file in the framework package as 'Help<Prefix>' string vars plus a 'Help(path ...string) (string, error)' resolver. Existing files are never overwritten — the help text is yours to edit.

dir.description: Subdirectory under the framework package where the per-command help .txt files live and are embedded. Files are seeded once when missing and are otherwise user-owned; rotini never rewrites or deletes them.

package.description: Import path (relative to module root) for the command handler package. Package name is derived from the last path segment.

gen_file.description: Name of the framework-controlled gen file placed in the command handler package (e.g. 'handlers.gen.go'). Must end in .go.

PruneConfig.description: Controls pruning of stub files in the command handler package.

enabled.description: When true, rotini removes stub files in the command handler package that no longer correspond to a command in the spec.

keep.description: File names (not paths) that should never be removed by pruning, even when they do not correspond to a command in the spec.

package.description: Import path (relative to module root) for the framework package. Package name is derived from the last path segment.

gen_file.description: Name of the framework gen file placed in the framework package (e.g. 'rotini.gen.go'). Must end in .go.

additional_imports.description: Additional Go import paths included in the generated framework file. Use when input or output types reference third-party packages. Each entry is a package path (e.g., 'net/url') or an aliased import (e.g., 'myalias net/url').
